entries.name: Skill Checks & Attribute Requirements
entries.content:
In the world of Bangresh, all actions are governed by attributes and skills. Whether one is casting powerful spells, negotiating with a cunning merchant, or surviving in the harsh wilderness, skill checks determine success or failure.

Skill checks in Bangresh follow a simple system:

• Base Roll: A d20 is rolled.

• Modifiers: Attributes and skills provide bonuses or penalties.

• Success Threshold: Rolls 11 or higher succeed, while 10 or lower fail.

• Critical Success (20+): Extraordinary success beyond normal capability.

• Critical Failure (1 or lower): Disastrous failure with consequences.

🔷 Modifiers & Influence
Modifiers are based on a combination of Attributes + Skills:

• Higher Attributes → Stronger Baseline Competency

• Higher Skill Level → Greater Mastery & Unique Perks

• Environmental & Circumstantial Effects → Context matters (e.g., fighting in darkness, a slippery surface, exhaustion).

Certain tasks require specific attributes and skill checks:

• Essentia Checks: Absorbing unstable Essentia requires an Essentia Attunement (ESS) check, or the user risks unpredictable effects.

• Economic Checks: Bartering or Persuasion checks can determine whether a character avoids being scammed or uncovers rare opportunities.

• Combat Feats: Special maneuvers—such as counterattacks, grappling an enemy, or resisting knockback—rely on a combination of Might, Dexteria, and skill level.

Companion Assistance:

If a character lacks a required skill, a companion may assist, using their own attributes for the attempt.

entries.name: Character Growth & Progression
entries.content:
Leveling System:

1. Initiate (Lv. 1-9): Characters specialize in a single path, unlocking basic proficiencies.

2. Adept (Lv. 10-19): Advanced techniques become available, and hybrid class options emerge.

3. Expert (Lv. 20-29): The character refines their craft, unlocking powerful techniques and Essentia-based skills.

4. Master (Lv. 30-39): The pinnacle of normal growth—characters gain legendary abilities.

5. Ascendant (Lv. 40+): The realm of myths and gods, where power transcends mortals.

entries.name: Geistwalkers (Spiritual Augmentation Class)
entries.content:
"The dead do not sleep. They fight beside me."

Geistwalkers allow spirits, gods, or past ancestors to manifest around them like spectral armor, weapons, or extensions of their will.

Abilities:

• Spirit Manifestation – Summon a spirit to fight alongside or through them.

• Adaptive Enhancement – Different spirits grant different bonuses (defense, speed, offense, etc.).

• Ethereal Parry – Block attacks by shifting between the physical and spiritual plane.


• Subclasses: 

• Phantom Vanguards – Manifest warrior spirits to bolster defense and form ghostly armor.

• Wraithstrikers – Focuses on speed and precision, summoning ethereal blades and striking through foes.

• Echocallers – Summons multiple past spirits, forming a spectral army to overwhelm enemies.

Potential Users: Reshinel (due to their dual-nature), Urin (ancestral spirits of fallen warriors), and elite human warrior sects.

🏛 Societal Role: Highly respected in Urin warbands, where fallen ancestors are venerated. Elite Reshinel sects use them as spiritual advisors and warriors.

Training & Mastery Locations:

The Spectral Maw (where the strongest spirits are bound and tested)

The Shrine of Eternal Whispers (a resting place where the dead still speak)

The Phantom Arena (battleground where warriors duel their own past selves)

Legendary Figures:

Yurei the Unforgotten – Summoned an entire army of fallen heroes.

The Shade King – Became a spirit himself, fighting alongside his past lives.

Vorrak the Soulforged – Fused with his ancestral spirits permanently.

entries.name: Worldbinders (Environmental Casters)
entries.content:
"I do not wield magic. I am the magic of the land."

Magic users who don’t cast spells traditionally, but instead "bind" themselves to their environment, channeling the land’s magic as their own.

Abilities:

• Land Pact – Absorb magical properties from the terrain (fire in deserts, frost in tundras, gravity shifts in Floating Copse).

• Elemental Shift – Change how their magic manifests depending on the biome.

• Rooted Empowerment – The longer they stay in one place, the stronger they get.

Potential Users: Gangresh (plant-like beings), Gravetouched (gravity distorters), and Sul’Hari (desert survivalists).

🌿 Societal Role: Considered sages of the wild, revered by Gangresh tribes and feared by those who exploit nature.

Training & Mastery Locations:

The Verdant Shrine (deep in the heart of an ancient, sentient forest)

The Sunken Vaults (where drowned magic reshapes reality)

The Floating Copse (a gravity-defying forest in the sky)

Legendary Figures:

The Rootbound Sage – Became a living tree, still watching over the land.

Frostseer Khari – Controlled entire tundras with a single thought.

The Firewalker – Never burned, even as the inferno became his home.

entries.name: Veilcutters (Reality-Bending Thieves)
entries.content:
"To move unseen is skill. To move unfelt is art."

Stealth specialists who use magic to "slice" through reality, moving unseen, influencing minds, and striking with unnatural precision.

Abilities:

• Reality Slice – Cut through thin dimensional seams to bypass walls, traps, or appear behind foes.

• Word of the Forgotten – Enchant speech to implant suggestions, distort truth, or erase memories.

• Soul Gambit – Deal high physical & mental damage but at the cost of burning their own life force.

Potential Users: Ryatus-worshippers, Yisyoo (foxlike subspecies), and elite underground factions.

🕵️ Societal Role:
Operatives of Ryatus-worshipping assassins, feared members of the criminal underworld, and spies embedded in royal courts. Veilcutters are both revered and feared, known for their ability to slip through time and space unnoticed.

🔪 Training & Mastery Locations:

The Shroud Markets – Hidden black markets that phase in and out of reality, training Veilcutters in secrecy, deception, and the art of the Word of the Forgotten.

The Rift-Sewn Sanctum – A temple to Ryatus where assassins meditate in the void, learning to slice through dimensions.

The Sunless Alley – An underground network where only whispers remain, known for its brutal survival-based training.

⚔️ Legendary Figures:

Lazran "The Hollow Blade" – A Veilcutter who erased his own existence from history, appearing only to kill before vanishing again.

Yelka of the Silent Dawn – A Yisyoo thief who once infiltrated the celestial vaults of the gods.

Shade-Touched Viyrek – A man who was cut from reality itself, now existing in half-formed fragments across Bangresh.

entries.name: Pactborn (Faith-Based Class with Divine Contracts)
entries.content:
"A promise to a god is never broken—only paid in full."

Rather than just worshipping a god, Pactborn make direct deals with deities, gaining temporary but potent abilities based on their devotion.

Abilities:

• Divine Boon – Short-term access to god-like power (e.g., Adamanti grants impenetrable defense, Ryatus grants shadow-teleportation).

• Sacrificial Exchange – Exchange something (memories, blood, years of life) for greater power.

• Broken Oath – Severe punishment if they break a deal with a god.

Potential Users: Reshinel (highly attuned to divine forces), human priesthoods, secret cults.

🙏 Societal Role:
Found among priesthoods, cults, and divine warriors, Pactborn wield terrifying power but are often ostracized for their direct dealings with deities. Even the faithful fear those who bargain too closely with gods.

📜 Training & Mastery Locations:

The Shrine of Eternal Oaths – A sanctum where Pactborn train under divine scrutiny, forging contracts with gods.

The Cathedral of Silent Echoes – A place where whispers of long-dead gods still bargain for souls.

The Blood Pact Hall – An underground cult chamber where Pactborn undergo trials of sacrifice to unlock forbidden powers.

⚖️ Legendary Figures:

Rash the Twice-Bound – A Pactborn who made a deal with both Adamanti and Ryatus, balancing on the edge of divine contradiction.

Odelis the Forsworn – The only known Pactborn to break an oath and survive—though she now wanders as a cursed husk.

Vaspar of the Living Scripture – A priest who carved divine sigils into his own flesh, becoming a walking conduit for gods.

entries.name: Riftforged (Living Meteors)
entries.content:
"I was born in fire and fall only to rise again."

Hilohells (meteorite-born beings) who manipulate the cosmic energy that birthed them, using gravity, magnetism, and raw celestial force.

Abilities:

• Meteor Form – Momentarily shift into a comet-like body, crashing through enemies.

• Gravity Pulse – Increase or decrease gravity around themselves or others.

• Celestial Embers – Burn enemies with stellar radiation.

Potential Users: Exclusively Hilohells (racial class).

⚡ Societal Role:
Riftforged are divine beings to some and harbingers of destruction to others. They are worshipped by cults, feared by civilizations, and often left wandering, never truly belonging to the world of mortals.

☄️ Training & Mastery Locations:

The Hollow Crater – A massive impact site where Riftforged first awaken, surrounded by celestial energies.

The Starshatter Monastery – A floating temple where Riftforged hone control over their cosmic power.

The Black Sky Spire – A fortress at the edge of the world where Riftforged train in gravitational warfare.

🔥 Legendary Figures:

Tarkas the Falling Sun – A Riftforged who crashed through an empire’s capital, wiping out an entire dynasty in a single impact.

Zenka the Starbound – A Riftforged who rejected destruction, instead becoming a cosmic healer, using celestial embers to mend instead of burn.

Orros, the Weight of the World – A being so heavy with power that he warped gravity wherever he walked.

entries.name: Essentiamage (Enhanced Mage)
entries.content:
"Magic is not cast. It is written into the world."

• Mages aren’t just spellcasters—they manipulate Essentia, the raw energy of Bangresh.

• Spells are cast through sigils, requiring tracing motions or spoken incantations.

• Three paths: Runescribes (enchanted inscriptions), Essentiaborn (natural magic prodigies), and Channelers (focused elemental mastery).

📜 Societal Role:
Unlike traditional wizards, Essentiamages don’t just cast spells—they manipulate reality itself. They are sought after as scholars, warriors, and prophets, their power revered and feared in equal measure.

📖 Training & Mastery Locations:

The Archive of Lost Sigils – A vast underground library where forgotten spells and runes are rediscovered.

The Elemental Crucible – A testing ground where Essentiamages refine raw Essentia into controlled spellwork.

The Obsidian Pillars – Monolithic structures where Essentiaborn awaken their latent power.

🔮 Paths & Legendary Figures:

Runescribes – Masters of enchanted inscriptions. (Ex. Velran the Eternal, who bound his own soul into a single rune.)

Essentiaborn – Natural magic prodigies. (Ex. Kythea the Wildborn, whose mere presence reshaped the land.)

Channelers – Focused elemental wielders. (Ex. Orrik the Stormbinder, who pulled lightning from the heavens at will.)

entries.name: Sentinel (Enhanced Tank/Defender)
entries.content:
"I do not fall. I do not yield. I do not break."

• Instead of just blocking with a shield, they bind their soul to their armor, becoming a living fortress.

• Can absorb damage and unleash it in bursts, or become immovable objects on the battlefield.

🏰 Societal Role:
Sentinels are more than knights—they are the last line of defense in any battle, the ones who stand when all others fall. They serve as guardians, warlords, and champions of nations.

🛡️ Training & Mastery Locations:

The Unbroken Bastion – A fortress where Sentinels train in endurance, facing storms, fire, and relentless attack.

The Soulforge – An ancient forge where warriors bind their very essence to their armor.

The Immovable Keep – A monastery where warriors learn to become literal, living walls.

⚔️ Paths & Legendary Figures:

Ironbound – Pure defense. (Ex. Durak the Eternal, who once held off an entire army for seven days.)

Paragon – Protect allies. (Ex. Lady Veyla, the Unyielding Shield, who deflected an assassination attempt on a king by standing in the way of death itself.)

Juggernaut – Unstoppable force. (Ex. Borros the Mountain, who shattered siege engines with his bare hands.)

entries.name: Wanderer (Enhanced Rogue/Ranger)
entries.content:
"The road speaks, the wind whispers, and the stars guide."

• A nomadic class tied to the ley-lines of Bangresh, able to read the land and predict enemy movements.

• Uses spirit-touched arrows, stealthy movement, and environmental awareness.

🌍 Societal Role:
Wanderers are nomads, scouts, and survivalists, moving with the ley-lines of Bangresh. Some are mercenaries, some are monks, but all know that the land itself is their greatest ally.

🏹 Training & Mastery Locations:

The Silent Expanse – A place where ley-lines run wild, and Wanderers listen to the earth’s call.

The Moonlit Path – A secretive society of Ghostwalkers who move unseen, rumored to be phantoms.

The Cliffs of Horizon’s Edge – A sacred ground where Farseers hone their vision, seeing far beyond normal sight.

🌿 Paths & Legendary Figures:

Ghostwalkers – Stealth masters. (Ex. Jorin the Mistborn, who walked unseen even in broad daylight.)

Farseers – Snipers and visionaries. (Ex. Ailith the Unblinking, whose arrows never missed.)

Trailblazers – Speed-focused skirmishers. *(Ex. Harken of the Stormstride, who outran thunder itself.)

entries.name: The Adapter – The Ever-Shifting Blade
entries.content:
"A master of none is sometimes a master of all."

The Adapter is a combatant who refuses to be bound by a single style. They are trained in various disciplines, seamlessly blending melee, ranged, and magic into an unpredictable fighting style. Their strength is adaptability—though they never surpass true specialists in any one field, they excel at countering opponents by shifting tactics mid-battle.

🔹 Core Abilities:

      • Combat Morphing: Switches between different weapons, stances, and magic seamlessly.

      • Weakness Exploitation: Gains bonuses when targeting an enemy’s vulnerabilities.

      • Tactical Shift: Can adjust battle strategies mid-fight, making them difficult to predict.

🔹 Class Evolution Paths:

       • Polymath – Masters the art of blending knowledge from multiple disciplines, predicting enemy movements, and battlefield manipulation.

       • Omnistriker – Focuses on rapid attack chaining, switching between weapons and spells with fluidity.

       • Mimic Sage – Gains the ability to temporarily copy the techniques of opponents or allies.

🔹 Training & Mastery Locations:

       • The Wanderer’s Hall – A guild of battle-hardened mercenaries who teach adaptability over strict discipline.

       • The Twin Masters of Yin & Yang – Philosophers who believe that all combat forms originate from a single universal technique.

entries.name: The Summoner – The Keeper of the Forgotten Scrolls
entries.content:
"Within these ancient scrolls lie the echoes of gods, beasts, and warriors long erased from history."

Summoners wield powerful and forbidden artifacts known as Summoning Scrolls. These scrolls contain the names of legendary creatures, fallen warlords, and spirits exiled from history. Through their arcane knowledge, Summoners call forth these entities to aid them in battle, whether to attack, defend, or empower allies.

🔹 Core Abilities:

       • Summoning Scrolls: Calls forth powerful spirits, monsters, or warriors.

       • Ethereal Bonds: Some summoned creatures persist as passive buffs or protective spirits.

       • Arcane Seals: Must maintain control over powerful summons, or risk them breaking free.

🔹 Class Evolution Paths:

       • Spirit Caller – Specializes in summoning lost souls and spectral warriors.

       • Beastbinder – Masters summoning legendary creatures, riding and commanding them in battle.

       • Forbidden Archivist – Unlocks the knowledge of gods and calamities, summoning entities at great personal risk.

🔹 Training & Mastery Locations:

       • The Hidden Sanctum of the Exiled Scrollkeepers – A hidden monastery where summoners preserve ancient arts.

       • The Ashen Pillars – A ruined battleground where powerful spirits roam, waiting for one worthy to bind them.
entries.comment: The Summoner – The Keeper of the Forgotten Scrolls

entries.name: The Stiin – The Razor-Dancer’s Web
entries.content:
"What appears as a child’s toy is, in truth, an instrument of death."

The Stiin are precision-based warriors who use Stiin, a tool resembling razor-sharp strings, yo-yos, or wire-bound weapons. Their combat style is a dance of fluid movements, controlling the battlefield through traps, aerial maneuvers, and devastating momentum-based attacks.

🔹 Core Abilities:

       • Razor Webs: Creates a network of slicing strings to restrict enemy movement.

       • Momentum Combos: The longer a battle flows, the more powerful their strikes become.

       • Tether Manipulation: Latches onto enemies or objects to perform intricate attacks.

🔹 Class Evolution Paths:

       • String Reaper – Masters lethal execution techniques, making each movement a potential death sentence.

       • Webspinner – Specializes in trapping and controlling enemies with near-invisible threads.

       • Phantom Dancer – Blends acrobatics and illusions, creating afterimages and unpredictable movements.

🔹 Training & Mastery Locations:

       • The Silk Monastery – A hidden temple where monks teach the deadly art of Stiin combat.

       • The Marionette Guild – A sect of assassins who manipulate battle like puppeteers.

entries.name: The Qin – The Unyielding Counterforce
entries.content:
"I do not strike first. I simply wait for the world to break itself against me."

The Qin are a unique class that thrives on patience, absorbing an enemy’s force and redirecting it with devastating precision. Unlike other warriors, a Qin does not attack outright. Instead, they counter, waiting for the perfect moment to retaliate. However, when pushed to their limits, a Qin calls upon a forgotten god, transforming into an avatar of divine wrath.

🔹 Core Abilities:

       • Defensive Stance: Cannot attack first—must wait for an enemy’s move.

       • Rage Essence: Stores all damage taken and converts it into counterattacks.

       • Divine Awakening: When rage reaches its peak, the Qin transforms into an unstoppable force.

🔹 Class Evolution Paths:

       • Tranquil Guardian – Masters pure defensive counters, redirecting entire attacks back at opponents.

       • Wrath Incarnate – Specializes in Divine Awakening, becoming a relentless war machine.

       • Echo of the Forgotten God – Permanently bonds with divine power, gaining supernatural abilities.

🔹 Training & Mastery Locations:

       • The Silent Keep – A monastery where Qin train in patience, stillness, and the art of counterplay.

       • The Sealed Crater – The remains of an ancient battle where a god’s wrath still lingers.

entries.name: Training Grounds & Mastery Locations
entries.content:
• The Hall of Echoing Paths – A central hub where warriors of all disciplines gather to train and challenge each other.

• The Forbidden Vaults – A hidden archive containing lost knowledge of summoning, magic, and forbidden techniques.

• The Bloodstained Colosseum – A brutal proving ground where only the strongest warriors survive.

• The Shattered Monastery – A ruin where the last remnants of the Qin’s god still whisper to those who listen.

entries.name: Fame & Infamy (General Reputation Levels)
entries.content:
### **Fame & Infamy (General Reputation Levels)**  
Your reputation in **Bangresh** is not just a number—it shapes how the world perceives you and influences your interactions with NPCs, factions, and entire regions. Every action, from slaying a legendary beast to betraying an ally, leaves a mark on how you are treated.  

#### **🌟 Exalted (Living Legend)**  
- **The World’s Response:** You are a myth made flesh, a figure of inspiration or dread. Bards immortalize your deeds in song, monarchs offer you feasts in grand halls, and common folk may weep at the sight of you.  
- **Perks:**  
  - Nobles and rulers may seek alliances or offer land and titles.  
  - Some may try to manipulate you for political gain.  
  - Even enemies hesitate to challenge you outright.  
- **Faction & Local Impact:**  
  - **Tribes & Clans:** You are a chieftain in all but name. They may gift you sacred relics, marry into your lineage, or call upon you in times of great crisis.  
  - **Kingdoms & Factions:** You may be given command of armies or entrusted with governance over lands. Your influence could sway the outcome of wars.  
  - **Religious Orders:** Some may see you as divinely chosen, seeking to elevate you as a holy figure—or brand you as a heretic for defying their will.  

#### **✅ Venerated (Respected Icon)**  
- **The World’s Response:** Your name commands respect, even from those who despise you. Warriors toast in your honor, scholars seek your insights, and merchants may craft artifacts bearing your name.  
- **Perks:**  
  - Discounts from traders, access to hidden knowledge, and invitations to exclusive circles.  
  - The nobility may seek to sponsor you or entangle you in court politics.  
  - Rivals may try to tarnish your reputation.  
- **Faction & Local Impact:**  
  - **Tribes & Clans:** They tell stories of your deeds and may request your aid in sacred trials or hunts.  
  - **Kingdoms & Factions:** You may be offered official rank, military command, or diplomatic missions.  
  - **Religious Orders:** Some may petition you for blessings or invite you to sacred rites.  

#### **😐 Recognized (Known but Neutral)**  
- **The World’s Response:** Your name carries weight, but opinions vary. Some view you as a capable adventurer, while others remain skeptical of your true motives.  
- **Perks & Consequences:**  
  - You can move freely without excessive praise or condemnation.  
  - Commoners may ask for aid but won’t expect miracles.  
  - Some may still doubt your capabilities.  
- **Faction & Local Impact:**  
  - **Tribes & Clans:** You are a guest rather than kin—treated with respect but not reverence.  
  - **Kingdoms & Factions:** You are acknowledged but unimportant politically unless you prove otherwise.  
  - **Religious Orders:** They observe from a distance, judging whether you are worthy of their favor.  

#### **⚠️ Disreputable (Questionable Character)**  
- **The World’s Response:** Whispers follow you. Are you a rogue, an opportunist, or simply unlucky? Some suspect your motives, and paranoia creeps in among those who deal with you.  
- **Perks & Consequences:**  
  - Merchants may overcharge you.  
  - Guards might keep an eye on you.  
  - Your reputation could make it difficult to gain allies.  
- **Faction & Local Impact:**  
  - **Tribes & Clans:** They may challenge you to trials of honor to prove yourself.  
  - **Kingdoms & Factions:** You might be offered work, but it’s likely to be underhanded or dangerous.  
  - **Religious Orders:** Some may see you as needing redemption, while others shun you.  

#### **❌ Outlawed (Wanted Criminal)**  
- **The World’s Response:** You are no longer just distrusted—you are actively hunted. Guards may attack on sight, bounty hunters track your steps, and villages shut their gates against you.  
- **Perks & Consequences:**  
  - Some criminal groups might welcome you.  
  - Disguises and bribery may be necessary to function in society.  
  - Betrayal is a constant threat.  
- **Faction & Local Impact:**  
  - **Tribes & Clans:** Some might respect your defiance, but many will cast you out or challenge you.  
  - **Kingdoms & Factions:** You are officially an enemy of the state. Kingdoms may send assassins or war parties after you.  
  - **Religious Orders:** Purists may see you as a blight to be cleansed.  

#### **☠️ Cursed (Reviled or Worshiped as a Monster)**  
- **The World’s Response:** You are feared, hated, or worshiped in hushed voices. Townsfolk flee at your sight, vengeful families hunt you, and cults may rise in your name.  
- **Perks & Consequences:**  
  - Fear grants you power—some will obey simply to avoid your wrath.  
  - Cursed items, dark magic, or supernatural forces may be drawn to you.  
  - Most civilizations will not tolerate your presence.  
- **Faction & Local Impact:**  
  - **Tribes & Clans:** Some may declare blood feuds against you, while others may revere you as a dark spirit.  
  - **Kingdoms & Factions:** You may be a war criminal or the target of holy crusades.  
  - **Religious Orders:** Cults may form around you, while holy warriors seek to vanquish you.  

---

### **Faction & Local Reputation**  
Unlike your overall reputation, faction and local reputation dictate how specific groups perceive you. Some may honor the bold; others punish the reckless.

#### **Tribes & Clans (Honor & Survival-Based Societies)**  
- **High Reputation:** You may be adopted into their kin, given sacred relics, and asked to lead hunts or rituals.  
- **Low Reputation:** Exile, public shaming, or being hunted for dishonor.  

#### **Kingdoms & Noble Houses (Politics & Power)**  
- **High Reputation:** Access to courtly affairs, potential nobility status, and command over armies.  
- **Low Reputation:** Branded a traitor, stripped of rank, or executed.  

#### **Religious Orders (Faith & Purity)**  
- **High Reputation:** Seen as a prophet, saint, or chosen warrior. Given divine blessings or relics.  
- **Low Reputation:** Branded a heretic, excommunicated, or hunted.  

#### **Merchants & Guilds (Profit & Trustworthiness)**  
- **High Reputation:** Better trade deals, access to rare goods, and economic influence.  
- **Low Reputation:** Blacklisted, swindled, or outright banned from trade.  

#### **The Order of Ash (Rogue Mages & Forbidden Knowledge)**  
- **High Reputation:** Welcomed into the fold, given access to lost arcane knowledge.  
- **Low Reputation:** Considered a threat and marked for elimination.

entries.name: Bounty & Crime System (Law & Chaos in Bangresh)
entries.content:
Bangresh doesn’t have a universal police force—each region enforces its own justice.

• Petty Crimes (Pickpocketing, Trespassing) → Fines, bribes, or warnings.

• Serious Crimes (Murder, Treason, Forbidden Magic) → Bounties, exile, or execution.

• Escaping Justice (Bounty Hunter & Legal Impact)

• Bounty Too High? → Mercenaries & Hunters Will Track You

• Bribe the Right People? → You Might Walk Free

• Powerful Enough? → The Law Bends for You
entries.comment: Bounty & Crime System (Law & Chaos in Bangresh)

entries.name: NPC Memory & Dynamic Reactions
entries.content:
NPCs in Bangresh will not forget. Their opinions evolve based on history with you.

Memory-Based NPC Reactions:

• If you betray a village once… → They may forgive you if you compensate them.

• If you keep lying… → People stop trusting you, even when you tell the truth.

• If you kill someone’s kin… → They will not forget—even years later.

• If you rescue someone’s child… → They may become a lifelong ally.

entries.name: Morality & Choices
entries.content:
# **Morality & The Three Veils of the Soul**  

In **Bangresh**, morality is not a rigid system of good and evil but a reflection of choices, perceptions, and consequences. Every decision you make—whether noble, ruthless, or pragmatic—shapes how the world sees you, how factions react, and how the supernatural forces of the realm take notice.  

### **🌿 The Veil of Kin (Honor & Duty)**  
*How you uphold bonds—whether to family, tribe, or people.*  

- **High Kin Veil:** You are seen as loyal, dependable, and honorable. Those who value tradition and trust will stand by you, even in dire times.  
- **Low Kin Veil:** You are viewed as unreliable, self-serving, or even treacherous. Close allies may hesitate to trust you.  
- **Shattered Kin Veil:** You have broken sacred oaths, betrayed fundamental bonds, or turned against your own kin. Blood feuds, exile, or vengeance may follow.  

**🌀 Example Dilemmas & Consequences:**  
- **Redemption:** If you have shattered your Kin Veil, earning back trust may require grand gestures—risking your life, avenging past wrongs, or proving your loyalty through deep sacrifice.  
- **Betrayal:** Do you sell out your allies for a greater cause, knowing that even if you succeed, you will forever be branded a traitor?  

---

### **🔥 The Veil of Embers (Survival & Strength)**  
*How you respond to the harshness of Bangresh—do you conquer, endure, or crumble?*  

- **High Ember Veil:** You are seen as unbreakable—respected by warriors, feared by the weak, and sought after as a leader.  
- **Low Ember Veil:** You are perceived as weak, naive, or expendable. Some may try to use you or cast you aside.  
- **Shattered Ember Veil:** You have lost your will to fight. You are prey, marked by scavengers, predators, and those who feast on the weak.  

**🌀 Example Dilemmas & Consequences:**  
- **Corruption:** A forbidden power can make you stronger, but at what cost? If you embrace it, warriors may fear you, but your soul may never recover.  
- **Survival vs. Compassion:** Do you leave behind the wounded to save yourself, knowing it will make you stronger but cost you the respect of your allies?  

---

### **🩸 The Veil of Shadows (Morality & Perception of the Soul)**  
*How others interpret your morality—and whether divine or dark forces take notice.*  

- **High Shadow Veil:** You are a beacon of virtue—healers, spirits, and the righteous may be drawn to you.  
- **Low Shadow Veil:** You are feared, distrusted, or seen as ruthless. The wicked may seek your company, and some may attempt to use you.  
- **Shattered Shadow Veil:** You are a walking curse—worshiped by the damned, hunted by the divine, and forever marked by the abyss.  

**🌀 Example Dilemmas & Consequences:**  
- **Moral Temptation:** Will you sacrifice innocent lives for the power to change the world, knowing that once you cross the line, you may never return?  
- **Divine vs. Dark Influence:** A high Shadow Veil may earn you divine blessings—but also make you a target for demons seeking corruption. A shattered veil could twist your very being, causing supernatural horrors to unfold.  

---

## **Dynamic Morality: Choices, Redemption & Corruption**  
Rather than a static alignment system, Bangresh’s morality is shaped by choices, actions, and their ripple effects.  

### **🛠 Redemption is Possible—But Never Easy**  
- A fallen warrior who abandoned his allies must prove his loyalty through **sacrifice**, not words.  
- A warlord who seeks forgiveness may find that some **never forget** his atrocities.  
- Some crimes **cannot be undone**—there will always be those who seek vengeance.  

### **🩸 Corruption is Tempting—But Comes at a Cost**  
- Forbidden magic grants power, but **twists the soul**—even allies may question your path.  
- If you embrace the abyss, **the world will take notice**—some will worship you, others will seek to end you.  

### **⚖️ Moral Dilemmas That Shape the World**  
- **Protecting the Innocent vs. Betraying Your Comrades:** Will you uphold justice, even if it means turning against those who once stood by your side?  
- **Mastering the Arcane vs. Sacrificing Your Soul:** Will you make a pact with dark forces for forbidden knowledge, knowing it will forever mark you?  
- **Upholding Values vs. Achieving Your Goals:** Will you compromise your ideals for the greater good, or remain steadfast—even if it means failure?  

### **👥 Relationship Impacts**  
- **Teammates & Allies:** Your moral choices can inspire loyalty, provoke betrayal, or spark open conflict.  
- **Family & Kin:** Your actions may strengthen bonds—or lead to exile, blood feuds, or worse.  
- **Factions & Kingdoms:** Your reputation will shape whether you are seen as a hero, a tyrant, or something in between.  
- **The Divine & The Damned:** Whether you walk in light or shadow, greater forces will take notice—and their response may define your fate.  

---

### **The Living Morality of Bangresh**  
This system ensures that morality is not just a number or a rigid karma meter. Instead, it **organically evolves** based on actions, consequences, and perception—forcing players to navigate the **grey, often brutal, reality of Bangresh**.

entries.name: Advanced Combat & Skill Interactions
entries.content:
• Limb-Based Damage & Injuries:

Players and NPCs can suffer broken bones, bleeding wounds, or concussions requiring specific healing methods.

Examples:
Blunt force can break bones, lowering movement speed.
Bleeding wounds require bandages or coagulant magic, or the player slowly bleeds out.

• Skill Synergy & Multi-Classing:

Magic & Weapon Combinations – Players can combine abilities dynamically, leading to deep customization.

Examples:
Fire + Wind Magic = Explosion Magic
Earth + Water Magic = Mud that slows enemies
Sword + Lightning Magic = Faster attack speed and stun chance

• Mounted Combat & Creature Taming:

Players can ride creatures that have unique combat abilities.

Examples:
Taming a Skythorn (giant hawk) allows for aerial combat.
Riding a Thulbrak Beast (massive tundra creature) grants extra durability in cold regions.

entries.name: Psychological Warfare
entries.content:
**• Psychological Warfare:**

Characters can develop temporary or long-term effects from traumatic combat experiences, affecting their stats, relationships, forcing them to acquire cursed items, or even altering their perception of reality.

*   **Temporary Effects:**
    *   **Shock:** Lowers stamina for a few rounds.
        *   *Simple:* Stumbling, dazed expression.
        *   *Advanced:* Vomiting, uncontrollable shaking.
        *   *Chaotic:* Temporary blindness, deafness.
    *   **Rage:** Increases MGT but lowers MND for a few rounds.
        *   *Simple:* Increased aggression, reckless attacks.
        *   *Advanced:* Berserker state, immune to pain but unable to distinguish friend from foe.
        *   *Chaotic:* Uncontrollable laughter, spontaneous combustion.
    *   **Fear:** Reduces attack and defense against specific enemy types.
        *   *Simple:* Hesitation, trembling hands.
        *   *Advanced:* Panic attack, fleeing from combat.
        *   *Chaotic:* Catatonia, paralysis.
*   **Long-Term Effects:**
    *   **Phobias:** Lowers MND in specific environments or situations.
        *   *Simple:* Unease, discomfort.
        *   *Advanced:* Panic attacks, debilitating anxiety.
        *   *Chaotic:* Delusions, paranoia.
    *   **Nightmares:** Disrupts sleep, reducing stamina recovery.
        *   *Simple:* Restless sleep, tossing and turning.
        *   *Advanced:* Vivid and disturbing dreams, waking up screaming.
        *   *Chaotic:* Sleepwalking, acting out nightmares in real life.
    *   **Personality Changes:** Alters relationship values with specific NPCs or factions.
        *   *Simple:* Increased irritability, withdrawal from social interactions.
        *   *Advanced:* Loss of empathy, difficulty forming emotional connections.
        *   *Chaotic:* Split personality, multiple conflicting identities.
*   **Cursed Items:**
    *   **Whispering Helm:** Grants bonus to Lore checks but slowly lowers MND.
        *   *Simple:* Faint whispers, unsettling dreams.
        *   *Advanced:* Constant voices, hallucinations.
        *   *Chaotic:* Loss of identity, complete mental breakdown.
    *   **Life-Draining Sword:** Grants bonus to MGT but drains VIT with each use.
        *   *Simple:* Fatigue, weakness.
        *   *Advanced:* Premature aging, physical deterioration.
        *   *Chaotic:* Rapid decay, turning to dust.
    *   **Blood-Soaked Amulet:** Grants bonus to Intimidation but lowers CHA with friendly NPCs.
        *   *Simple:* Increased aggression, difficulty forming relationships.
        *   *Advanced:* Paranoia, suspicion of betrayal.
        *   *Chaotic:* Uncontrollable bloodlust, attacking allies.
*   **Environmental Triggers:**
    *   *Claustrophobia (Caves):* Increased anxiety, panic attacks.
    *   *Agoraphobia (Open Spaces):* Fear of leaving safe areas, reduced movement speed.
    *   *Haunted Locations:* Visions, whispers, feelings of dread.
*   **Social Manipulation:**
    *   *Guilt-Tripping:* Lowers target's resolve, making them more susceptible to persuasion.
    *   *Gaslighting:* Distorts target's perception of reality, making them question their sanity.
    *   *Divide and Conquer:* Sows discord among allies, turning them against each other.
*   **Random Mutations:**
    *   *Split Personality:* Character develops multiple conflicting identities, each with their own stats and abilities.
    *   *Altered Perception:* Character sees the world in a completely different way, gaining new insights but losing touch with reality.
    *   *Physical Deformities:* Character's body is twisted and warped, granting new abilities but also inflicting permanent penalties.

entries.name: Unique Endgame & Meta Mechanics
entries.content:
• Godhood & Ascension Paths:

Players can become gods, legends, or eternal figures if they leave enough of a mark.

Examples:
A player who masters an element might ascend to a minor elemental deity.
A player who dies epically may be worshiped as a martyr, gaining posthumous influence.

• True Open-Ended Endgame:

No forced endings – Players shape the world forever through their choices.

Examples:
Become a ruler of a faction and lead wars against others.
Become a wandering myth, appearing only when history calls for a hero or villain.

• Mythology System & Player Legacy:

Players’ stories become legends and influence future generations.

Examples:
NPCs in later eras tell conflicting tales of what the player did, leading to divergent myths.

entries.name: The Dominator Class
entries.content:
### **Dominator Class - The Forbidden Path of Subjugation**

#### **Class Overview**
The **Dominator** is not a class that can be chosen—it is **bestowed** or **forced upon the worthy**. Those who walk the path of Domination do not lead through words, nor do they bargain for loyalty. Instead, they claim absolute control through **raw power, combat supremacy, and supernatural subjugation**. To become a Dominator is to wield an authority so profound that even the mightiest creatures bend the knee—or die resisting.

A Dominator is the **pinnacle of melee superiority**, combining overwhelming strength with supernatural control over bound entities. They break the wills of the strong and forge unshakable chains of servitude, but each conquest brings them closer to the abyss of their own undoing. **Domination is not without risk**—the very creatures they control may one day seek to consume them.

---

#### **Origins & Legacy**
The first Dominators were warriors who sought to tame the world’s greatest beasts. They balanced power and control, but legends tell of a **cataclysmic betrayal**—an entity so powerful that even Dominators themselves fell to its rule. In their desperation, the last of them sealed away their knowledge, scattering the art of Domination into the most perilous corners of **Bangresh**.

##### **The Last Order of Domination**
The final Dominators did not perish in battle, nor did they fade into obscurity. Instead, they **disappeared**, their fates unknown. Some believe they now walk among mortals in secrecy, waiting for the right moment to **return**. Others claim they succumbed to their own power, transforming into **the very monsters they sought to command**.

---

#### **The Forbidden Pact: How a Dominator is Chosen**
Becoming a Dominator is not a simple choice—it is an **event**, an irreversible transformation. The methods vary, but all Dominators share one thing in common: they are **marked by something beyond themselves**.

##### **Methods of Awakening**
- **A Beast’s Submission:** A creature of immense power willingly submits, forging an unbreakable bond.
- **The Hollow Maw’s Trial:** Surviving the trials of **the Hollow Maw** and binding one of its ancient titans.
- **A Whisper from the Veil:** Spirits of the **Whispering Veil** mark the Dominator as their vessel.
- **The Shattering of Rynnix’s Chains:** When **Rynnix**, the bound dragon-hatchling, unbinds their first seal, the Dominator’s true power awakens.

---

#### **Combat Style & Core Mechanics**
A Dominator is a **brutal frontline enforcer**, blending mastery of melee combat with supernatural subjugation. Unlike tacticians who command armies, Dominators **conquer individuals**, overwhelming foes before chaining them into servitude.

##### **Core Mechanics:**
- **Brutal Subjugation:** Foes must be defeated through **combat superiority** before submission is possible.
- **Essentia Chains:** A binding strike—once an enemy weakens, the Dominator can forge an **Essentia Chain**, linking their souls.
- **Overpowering Aura:** Presence alone exerts dominance, making weaker enemies hesitate or falter.
- **Adaptive Mastery:** A Dominator gains **temporary boons** from subdued creatures, such as increased speed, regeneration, or elemental resistance.

##### **Signature Combat Style – The Law of Dominion**
A fusion of raw brutality and precise control, incorporating:
- **Grappling & Bone-Crushing Strikes** (Close Combat Supremacy)
- **Empowered Slams & Shockwave Attacks** (Area Control)
- **Chain-Based Combat** (Weapon Mastery)

---

#### **Subclasses of Domination**
Dominator specialization depends on the types of creatures they subjugate:

1. **Toadic Conqueror** – Amphibious specialist; controls creatures of **swamps and marshlands**.
2. **Titan Tamer** – Brute specialist; commands **great apes, Verdant Brutes, and colossal beasts**.
3. **Mermaid Master** – Aquatic specialist; rules **oceanic and river-dwelling entities**.
4. **Nimbus Overlord** – Aerial specialist; commands **levitating or sky-based creatures**.
5. **Siren Sovereign** – Spectral specialist; bends **ghosts, wraiths, and echoes to their will**.

---

#### **Weapons of the Dominator**
Every Dominator wields a **custom weapon**, forged from the **Essentia of their first conquest**. This weapon evolves over time, unlocking new powers based on **subjugated foes**.

##### **The User Can Choose From:**
- **The Tyrant’s Chains** – Twin **serrated chains** that extend and constrict, binding foes mid-battle.
- **The Warbrand of Conquest** – A massive, **runed greatsword** that feeds on the will of the conquered.
- **The Behemoth’s Maw** – A **colossal gauntlet** forged from the remains of a fallen titan, capable of crushing foes in a single grasp.
- **The Emperor’s Fang** – A **curved greatblade**, allowing rapid strikes and execution-based domination.
- **The Hollow Crown** – A **floating set of spectral blades**, controlled telekinetically by the Dominator’s will.

---

#### **Rynnix, the Bound Hatchling**
All Dominators are accompanied by **Rynnix**, a **small, dragon-like humanoid** bound in **arcane seals**. They cannot speak at first, but over time, they awaken.

##### **Growth Stages:**
1. **Chained Hatchling** – Can sense **hostility and weak points** in enemies.
2. **Awakened Warden** – Gains **limited control** over subjugated creatures.
3. **Unshackled** – Learns to **speak and challenge the Dominator’s decisions**.
4. **???** – Unknown. Only **legendary Dominators** have seen this form.

---

#### **The Laws of Domination & Risks**
- **Essentia Drain:** The stronger the dominated creature, the greater the toll on the Dominator’s **Essentia**.
- **Loyalty Thresholds:** Beasts and entities have **loyalty meters** that determine their willingness to follow commands.
- **Rebellion & Betrayal:** If pushed too far, creatures may **turn on their master**, becoming unchained threats.
- **Subjugation Rites:** Each creature has a unique **ritual of binding**, often requiring battle, sacrifice, or sheer willpower.

---

#### **Notable Figures & Legends**
- **Vexor the Ironsoul** – A Dominator who bound an **ancient celestial titan**, only to vanish mysteriously.
- **The Chainmother** – A nameless Dominator who enslaved entire **realms** before being devoured by her own creations.
- **Rynnix’s Lost Master** – Said to be the last Dominator before the fall of their order, their fate remains unknown.

---

### **Final Note**
It is whispered that **true Dominators** never die. Instead, they become **part of their greatest conquest**, bound eternally to the throne of their dominion. But should a Dominator ever **unleash the entity that ended their order**, Bangresh itself may crumble under its rule.

entries.name: The Orbwyn Class
entries.content:
### **Orbwyn Class - The Wailing Core, The Lyast Iorb**

#### **Class Overview**
The **Orbwyn** is a living conduit of **Mind (MIN) and Essentia (ESS)**, a being whose very existence is intertwined with the raw forces of magic. Marked by **Lyast**, radiant orbs embedded within their body, they are both **walking cataclysms and fragile enigmas**. An Orbwyn does not cast spells like ordinary mages; they **channel magic directly**, reshaping reality through sheer will.

However, this power comes at a cost—**Orbwyns are the ultimate glass cannons**. When pushed to their limits, their **Lyast awaken**, unleashing overwhelming destruction. But every use of their power brings them closer to collapse, as their bodies struggle to contain the energy they wield.

Among warriors, they are called the **Lyast Iorb—Last Light**. Among scholars, they are the **Wailing Core**, for their energy is said to howl like a vengeful storm before obliteration.

---

#### **The Nature of Lyast**
The **Lyast** are not mere magical orbs; they are **living fragments of Essentia**, bound to the Orbwyn’s soul. Each Lyast amplifies their power, but also **fragments their stability**. The more an Orbwyn channels their magic, the closer they come to unraveling.

##### **Lyast Activation:**
- In moments of **dire peril**, the Lyast surge with energy, exponentially increasing magical output.
- Each Lyast has an **Affliction Threshold**—exceeding it causes backlash, mental degradation, or bodily collapse.
- Ancient texts suggest Lyast are **not natural**, but remnants of an event that reshaped Bangresh.

---

#### **The Burden of Power**
Orbwyns do not choose their path—they are **born or created**. Most do not live long; either their unstable bodies fail them, or they are **hunted by forces that seek to erase them**.

Some say Orbwyns are the **remnants of a lost civilization**, their Lyast the only surviving fragments of an empire swallowed by its own magic. Others whisper that they are **weapons of forgotten gods**, abandoned to wander Bangresh as shattered echoes of divine will.

---

#### **The Laws of the Lyast Iorb**
To wield Lyast is to **burn brightly and fade quickly**. Their power is governed by strict limitations:

##### **Core Mechanics:**
- **Lyast Overload:** Surpassing magical thresholds can cause a **fracture**, leading to backlash, power loss, or instant death.
- **Essentia Hunger:** Orbwyns require massive amounts of **Essentia** to function. Without it, they deteriorate rapidly.
- **Shattered Awakening:** An Orbwyn can **sacrifice their stability** to unleash catastrophic power—but doing so shortens their lifespan.
- **Resonance Effect:** When multiple Orbwyns are near each other, their Lyast harmonize, creating unpredictable **reality-distorting fields**.

---

#### **Orbwyn Combat & Abilities**
Unlike traditional mages, an Orbwyn does not rely on incantations. Instead, they **channel magic through their Lyast**, shaping destruction with mere thought.

##### **Combat Style:**
- **Lyast Projection:** Fires, manipulates, or detonates Lyast, creating high-speed magical barrages.
- **Essentia Manipulation:** Converts raw Essentia into **shields, weapons, or annihilating pulses**.
- **Phase Flux:** Shifts their body into an ethereal state, avoiding damage but increasing instability.
- **Last Light Invocation:** When near death, all Lyast activate at once, granting overwhelming power for a brief moment before collapse.

---

#### **Subclasses of the Orbwyn**
Each Orbwyn adapts their unstable power in unique ways:

1. **Voidflare Ascendant** – Masters of **instantaneous destruction**, capable of **erasing** foes in an instant.
2. **Eclipsed Herald** – Wielders of **dimensional manipulation**, shifting between planes to evade harm.
3. **Starborn Cataclyst** – Celestial Orbwyns who tap into the **Veil of Riven Stars**, unlocking **cosmic devastation**.
4. **Lyast Requiem** – Masters of **self-destruction**, able to **detonate** themselves and regenerate from residual Essentia.
5. **Echoing Vestige** – Orbwyns whose fractured Lyast allow them to **exist across multiple moments in time**.

---

#### **Weapons of the Orbwyn**
While the Lyast themselves are their primary weapons, an Orbwyn may wield artifacts attuned to their instability.

##### **The User Can Choose From:**
- **The Wailing Core** – A crystalline staff that amplifies Lyast projections while absorbing backlash.
- **The Fractured Halo** – A floating ring of Lyast fragments, orbiting the user and striking at enemies independently.
- **The Howling Gauntlet** – A reinforced conduit, allowing the Orbwyn to **punch through reality itself**.
- **The Veilshard Blade** – A sword made from a broken Lyast, capable of **slicing through magical constructs**.
- **The Entropic Crown** – A cursed artifact that stabilizes Lyast—but at the cost of draining the user’s soul.

---

#### **Xeyth, the Fractured Echo** *(Special Ally)*
All Orbwyns are haunted by **Xeyth**, a **sentient Lyast fragment** that lingers near them. Xeyth is neither ally nor enemy—it is **a mirror of their instability**, whispering truths only the Orbwyn can hear.

##### **Growth Stages:**
1. **Flickering Remnant** – Xeyth appears as a shifting, voiceless orb, reacting to the Orbwyn’s emotions.
2. **Awakened Echo** – Gains the ability to **warn the Orbwyn of imminent collapse**.
3. **Sentient Resurgence** – Xeyth begins speaking, offering cryptic guidance—or manipulation.
4. **???** – In the legends of lost Orbwyns, there are tales of Xeyth **taking form**, becoming something **beyond an echo**.

---

#### **The Sanctuaries of the Orbwyn**
Most Orbwyns perish before they can seek refuge, but some have left behind **hidden sanctuaries**, places where their kind may survive.

##### **1. The Fractured Hollow** (*A Ruin of Forgotten Echoes*)
- A broken realm where Orbwyns once sought to **stabilize themselves**.
- The walls hum with memories of past Orbwyns, their energy still lingering.
- Ancient devices called **Lyast Reforgers** exist here, capable of temporarily mending damaged Lyast.

##### **2. The Veil of Riven Stars** (*A Gateway to Pure Essentia*)
- A celestial plane where **Lyast glow brightest**, allowing Orbwyns to transcend their limitations.
- Many who enter never return, becoming part of the Veil itself.
- The **Starborn Lyast**, a mythical artifact, is rumored to exist here, said to grant an Orbwyn control over their own fate.

---

#### **Unanswered Questions & Legends**
- **Who created the first Lyast?** Some claim they were stolen from **a divine being**, while others say they were **forged in a cataclysm**.
- **Why do their Lyast wail?** Scholars debate whether the sound is merely a magical effect or **something deeper—an echo of something that should never be heard**.
- **What lies beyond the Veil of Riven Stars?** Few Orbwyns have returned from it, and those who have **can no longer speak of what they saw**.

---

### **Final Note**
An Orbwyn does not live long. They either **burn out, collapse under their own power, or fade into legend**. And yet, in their final moments, they shine brighter than any other being on Bangresh, their **Last Light** illuminating the world **one final time**.

entries.name: The Intermist Class
entries.content:
### **Intermist Class - The Unseen Hand, The Mind’s Shadow**

#### **Class Overview**
The **Intermist** is not a warrior, nor a sorcerer—they are something far more dangerous. They are the voice behind the throne, the shadow that guides the blade, the presence that bends reality with nothing but a whisper. Unlike those who wield brute force or raw magic, the Intermist operates through **charisma, deception, and psychological warfare**. Their greatest weapons are **words**, their battlefield the **minds of those around them**.

An Intermist never commands. Instead, they make others believe their cause was their own all along. They do not fight; they make others fight in their place. And should the world crumble into war or unite in peace, it will have been their will all along—though none will know it.

---

#### **The Nature of an Intermist**
An Intermist does not seek direct power. They do not wear crowns, lead armies, or openly claim dominion. Instead, they pull the strings from behind the scenes, ensuring the rulers, warriors, and rebels all unknowingly serve their interests.

##### **Core Traits:**
- **The Art of Persuasion:** An Intermist’s words carry supernatural weight, turning allies into pawns and enemies into zealots.
- **The Power of Presence:** Even in silence, their existence alone shifts conversations, strategies, and alliances.
- **The Shadow Without Form:** An Intermist never stands in the spotlight. They ensure **someone else** takes credit for their victories—but remains forever in their debt.

---

#### **The Laws of Influence**
To manipulate is to walk a razor’s edge. The Intermist must balance power with subtlety, ensuring their hand remains unseen lest their web unravel.

##### **Core Mechanics:**
- **Silver Tongue:** Conversations with an Intermist always favor their interests, even when they shouldn’t.
- **Unseen Chains:** They can subtly guide their allies' actions without issuing direct commands.
- **The Grand Masquerade:** Their identity is fluid, seamlessly integrating into different factions and power structures.
- **The Long Con:** Their influence is not immediate—it grows over time, planting ideas that blossom into obedience.

---

#### **The Forbidden Voice: How an Intermist is Chosen**
One does not choose to be an Intermist. The path is **bestowed upon them**, often through a life-changing moment that opens their mind to the power of influence.

##### **Methods of Awakening:**
- **A Deal with the Gilded Veil:** An Intermist’s journey begins when they first use their words to **reshape fate itself**, gaining the attention of unseen forces.
- **The Hollow Whisper:** Some claim Intermists hear voices not of the living, but of **long-dead manipulators**, whispering the secrets of control.
- **The Fall of a King:** An Intermist is often born from a shattered system—when they realize they can control **not just people, but the very world itself**.
- **Echoes of the Forgotten:** Those who survive a trial within **the Hollow Forum** gain an understanding of how true power works—and how to wield it unseen.

---

#### **Abilities & Core Mechanics**
Intermists do not engage in direct combat. Their power lies in **undermining**, **redirecting**, and **redefining** the battlefield.

##### **Combat Style:**
- **Whispered Command:** The Intermist can plant a thought in an enemy’s mind, making them hesitate—or betray their own side.
- **Fabricated Reality:** They can manipulate perception, causing foes to see allies as threats or vice versa.
- **The Art of Escape:** An Intermist is never caught unprepared—should their influence fail, they vanish, leaving their pawns to suffer.
- **Gravitas:** Their mere presence forces others to second-guess their choices, steering them toward the Intermist’s intended outcome.

---

#### **Subclasses of the Intermist**
Each Intermist refines their approach, specializing in different aspects of control and deception:

1. **The Courtly Spider** – Masters of **political intrigue**, shaping kingdoms from the shadows.
2. **The Nameless One** – Identity is an illusion; they seamlessly **become** whoever they need to be.
3. **The Veiled Prophet** – Religious and spiritual manipulators, wielding **faith as a weapon**.
4. **The Black Harlequin** – Tricksters who specialize in **chaos, misdirection, and psychological warfare**.
5. **The Silent Director** – Grand strategists who orchestrate **wars, revolutions, and betrayals** without lifting a blade.

---

#### **Weapons of the Intermist**
An Intermist’s weapons are not tools of war, but **instruments of manipulation**, artifacts that enhance their ability to weave influence.

##### **The User Can Choose From:**
- **The Silver Quill** – A writing instrument imbued with ancient persuasion magic, causing contracts and decrees to favor the Intermist.
- **The Masquerade Mask** – Allows the Intermist to shift their identity, altering their **appearance, voice, and mannerisms** at will.
- **The Echoing Locket** – A cursed relic that lets the Intermist **mimic the voice** of anyone they’ve encountered.
- **The Hollow Coin** – When flipped, fate seems to favor the Intermist in all things.
- **The Veilbound Dagger** – A symbolic weapon, rarely used in battle but carrying the weight of silent authority. A single cut binds the victim to the Intermist’s will.

---

#### **Veynn, the Echoing Shade** *(Special Ally)*
All Intermists are shadowed by **Veynn**, an **illusory entity** that only they can see. Veynn is more than a companion—it is a **reflection of their own manipulative nature**, feeding off deception and half-truths.

##### **Growth Stages:**
1. **Whispering Shade** – Veynn can **echo voices** around the Intermist, allowing them to project false words.
2. **Mirage Twin** – Gains the ability to **briefly take on the Intermist’s appearance**, confusing enemies.
3. **Sentient Masquerade** – Develops independent thought, sometimes acting without the Intermist’s command.
4. **???** – Legends whisper of Intermists whose shadows **no longer follow them**, but instead **lead them**.

---

#### **The Sanctuaries of the Intermist**
Few places harbor Intermists openly, but whispers speak of hidden domains where influence reigns supreme.

##### **1. The Gilded Veil** (*The Den of Lies*)
- A place where deals are made, debts are forged, and nations are shaped in secret.
- The walls supposedly record every whisper, waiting for the right price to reveal them.

##### **2. The Hollow Forum** (*The Place of Forgotten Kings*)
- A ruined council chamber where the echoes of ancient rulers **still advise those who listen**.
- Some say the greatest Intermists never die—they merely fade into legend, their influence eternal.

---

#### **Unanswered Questions & Legends**
- **How many wars have they started—or prevented?**
- **Has an Intermist ever ruled openly, or do they always remain in the shadows?**
- **Can an Intermist ever truly be trusted, even by those closest to them?**
- **Are Intermists born, or made?** Some say their talents are learned. Others whisper that the greatest among them are simply... different.

---

### **Final Note**
It is said that true Intermists never fall from power, for their legacies **live on through those they have shaped**. And should an Intermist ever misstep, one must wonder—was it truly their failure, or merely **another step in their grand design**?

entries.content:
[🔓CLASSIC]:

**Diplomacy Skill Page: The Art of Influence and Negotiation**

This page details the core diplomacy skills available to characters in Bangresh, outlining their progression, specializations, and potential synergies. Mastery of these skills is essential for navigating the complex social and political landscape of the world, forging alliances, resolving conflicts, and achieving your goals through words rather than weapons.

**I. Core Diplomacy Skills:**

*   **Persuasion:** The ability to influence others through reasoned arguments, emotional appeals, and subtle manipulation.
    *   **Progression:** Novice -> Apprentice -> Journeyman -> Expert -> Grandmaster
    *   **Specializations:**
        *   **Rhetoric:** The art of public speaking and argumentation, used to sway large audiences and win debates.
            *   *Advanced Techniques:* Logical fallacies, emotional appeals, storytelling, charisma.
            *   *Synergies:* Leadership (for inspiring followers), Diplomacy (for negotiating treaties), Intimidation (for threatening opponents).
        *   **Negotiation:** The art of bargaining and compromise, used to reach mutually beneficial agreements and resolve conflicts peacefully.
            *   *Advanced Techniques:* Bluffing, concessions, win-win solutions, leverage.
            *   *Synergies:* Bartering (for economic negotiations), Diplomacy (for international relations), Deception (for manipulating opponents).
        *   **Charm:** The art of using personal appeal and charisma to win over individuals and build rapport.
            *   *Advanced Techniques:* Flattery, empathy, active listening, body language.
            *   *Synergies:* Deception (for creating false impressions), Intimidation (for subtle threats), Leadership (for inspiring loyalty).
    *   **Mastery Bonuses:** Each specialization grants unique bonuses at higher levels, such as increased success chance, improved dialogue options, or special social abilities.

*   **Deception:** The ability to mislead others through lies, disguises, and subtle manipulation.
    *   **Progression:** Novice -> Apprentice -> Journeyman -> Expert -> Grandmaster
    *   **Specializations:**
        *   **Bluffing:** The art of deceiving others in games of chance and social interactions, used to gain an advantage or avoid detection.
            *   *Advanced Techniques:* Reading tells, creating false impressions, exploiting vulnerabilities, maintaining composure.
            *   *Synergies:* Gambling (for winning games), Persuasion (for convincing others), Stealth (for avoiding detection).
        *   **Disguise:** The art of altering one's appearance to blend in with different groups or impersonate specific individuals.
            *   *Advanced Techniques:* Makeup, prosthetics, voice acting, mannerisms.
            *   *Synergies:* Stealth (for infiltration), Espionage (for gathering intelligence), Performance (for creating believable characters).
        *   **Manipulation:** The art of influencing others through subtle psychological tactics, used to control their actions and achieve your goals.
            *   *Advanced Techniques:* Gaslighting, guilt-tripping, emotional blackmail, divide and conquer.
            *   *Synergies:* Intimidation (for exerting control), Persuasion (for swaying opinions), Leadership (for building cults).
    *   **Mastery Bonuses:** Each specialization grants unique bonuses at higher levels, such as increased success chance, improved dialogue options, or special social abilities.

*   **Intimidation:** The ability to influence others through threats, fear, and displays of power.
    *   **Progression:** Novice -> Apprentice -> Journeyman -> Expert -> Grandmaster
    *   **Specializations:**
        *   **Coercion:** The art of forcing others to comply through direct threats and physical force.
            *   *Advanced Techniques:* Torture, blackmail, hostage-taking, violence.
            *   *Synergies:* Weapon Mastery (for physical dominance), Unarmed Combat (for close-quarters combat), Endurance (for withstanding resistance).
        *   **Subterfuge:** The art of using subtle threats and psychological tactics to instill fear and control.
            *   *Advanced Techniques:* Gaslighting, guilt-tripping, social isolation, character assassination.
            *   *Synergies:* Deception (for creating false impressions), Persuasion (for manipulating emotions), Espionage (for gathering compromising information).
        *   **Dominance:** The art of asserting authority and establishing control through displays of power and confidence.
            *   *Advanced Techniques:* Posturing, intimidation displays, social hierarchy, resource control.
            *   *Synergies:* Leadership (for commanding followers), Tactics (for strategic planning), Wealth (for economic influence).
    *   **Mastery Bonuses:** Each specialization grants unique bonuses at higher levels, such as increased success chance, improved dialogue options, or special social abilities.

**II. Secondary Diplomacy Skills:**

*   **Bartering:** The ability to negotiate favorable trades and economic deals.
    *   **Progression:** Novice -> Apprentice -> Journeyman -> Expert -> Grandmaster
    *   **Benefits:**
        *   Improved Prices: Allows you to buy goods for less and sell them for more.
        *   Resource Management: Enables you to acquire rare and valuable resources.
        *   Economic Influence: Allows you to manipulate markets and control trade routes.
        *   Wealth Accumulation: Enables you to amass vast fortunes and economic power.
    *   **Synergies:** Persuasion (for negotiating deals), Deception (for exploiting loopholes), Intimidation (for enforcing contracts).

*   **Lore:** The ability to recall historical events, cultural customs, and political relationships.
    *   **Progression:** Novice -> Apprentice -> Journeyman -> Expert -> Grandmaster
    *   **Benefits:**
        *   Cultural Understanding: Allows you to navigate different societies and avoid social faux pas.
        *   Political Awareness: Enables you to understand the motivations and goals of different factions.
        *   Historical Knowledge: Allows you to draw upon past events to inform your decisions and predict future outcomes.
        *   Secret Discovery: Enables you to uncover hidden information and ancient secrets.
    *   **Synergies:** Persuasion (for appealing to cultural values), Deception (for exploiting historical grievances), Intimidation (for threatening cultural taboos).

*   **Insight:** The ability to perceive subtle cues, read body language, and discern hidden intentions.
    *   **Progression:** Novice -> Apprentice -> Journeyman -> Expert -> Grandmaster
    *   **Benefits:**
        *   Lie Detection: Allows you to identify when someone is being dishonest.
        *   Emotional Awareness: Enables you to understand the emotions of others and respond appropriately.
        *   Motive Assessment: Allows you to determine the true motivations behind someone's actions.
        *   Hidden Agenda: Enables you to uncover secret plots and hidden agendas.
    *   **Synergies:** Persuasion (for tailoring your arguments), Deception (for concealing your own intentions), Intimidation (for exploiting vulnerabilities).

**III. Advanced Diplomacy Specializations:**

These specializations require significant investment in core diplomacy skills and offer unique social and political abilities.

*   **Spymaster:** A master of espionage and intelligence gathering, who manipulates events from the shadows and controls the flow of information.
    *   **Requirements:** High Deception, High Stealth, Moderate Lore.
    *   **Abilities:**
        *   Infiltration: Allows you to infiltrate secure locations and gather intelligence undetected.
        *   Manipulation: Enables you to control enemy agents and spread misinformation.
        *   Assassination: Allows you to eliminate key targets and destabilize enemy factions.
    *   **Playstyle:** Cunning, strategic, focused on controlling information and manipulating events from behind the scenes.

*   **Demagogue:** A charismatic orator who can sway the masses with fiery speeches and populist appeals, inspiring them to action and revolution.
    *   **Requirements:** High Persuasion, High Rhetoric, Moderate Intimidation.
    *   **Abilities:**
        *   煽動: Allows you to incite riots and rebellions among the populace.
        *   Propaganda: Enables you to spread misinformation and manipulate public opinion.
        *   Cult of Personality: Allows you to build a loyal following and establish a cult of personality.
    *   **Playstyle:** Charismatic, manipulative, focused on gaining power through popular support and social unrest.

*   **Negotiator:** A skilled diplomat who can broker peace treaties, forge alliances, and resolve conflicts between warring factions.
    *   **Requirements:** High Persuasion, High Negotiation, Moderate Lore.
    *   **Abilities:**
        *   Mediation: Allows you to facilitate negotiations between warring factions and reach mutually beneficial agreements.
        *   Alliance Building: Enables you to forge powerful alliances and unite disparate groups under a common banner.
        *   Peace Treaty: Allows you to negotiate lasting peace treaties and prevent future conflicts.
    *   **Playstyle:** Diplomatic, strategic, focused on achieving peace and stability through negotiation and cooperation.

**IV. Diplomacy Skill Synergies:**

Combining different diplomacy skills can create powerful synergies and unlock unique social and political strategies. Here are a few examples:

*   **Charismatic Deceiver:** Combines Persuasion (Charm) [🔓CLASSIC]:

with Deception (Bluffing) to create a charming liar who can manipulate others with ease. They can win over their targets with flattery and false promises, then exploit their trust for personal gain.

*   **Intimidating Negotiator:** Combines Persuasion (Negotiation) with Intimidation (Coercion) to create a ruthless negotiator who can get what they want through a combination of persuasion and threats. They can offer their opponents a fair deal, but if they refuse, they will not hesitate to resort to violence or blackmail.

*   **Knowledgeable Manipulator:** Combines Deception (Manipulation) with Lore to create a cunning manipulator who can exploit the fears and prejudices of others. They can use their knowledge of history and culture to sow discord and incite conflict, or to build alliances and consolidate power.

*   **Insightful Leader:** Combines Persuasion (Rhetoric) with Insight to create an inspiring leader who can connect with their followers on an emotional level. They can use their understanding of human nature to motivate their followers to achieve great things, or to manipulate them into blindly following their orders.

These are just a few examples of the many possible diplomacy skill synergies. By combining different skills, players can create unique and powerful characters who can shape the world of Bangresh through their words and actions. Remember, the pen is mightier than the sword, but a well-placed lie can be even more effective.

**I. Esoteric Arts (Merging Esoteric & Spiritual Skills, Psionic/Mental Skills, and Essentia Arts):**

This skill tree focuses on manipulating the unseen forces of the world, bending reality, and influencing the minds of others. It draws upon spiritual energy, mental power, and the manipulation of Essentia.

*   **Progression:** Novice -> Apprentice -> Journeyman -> Expert -> Grandmaster
*   **Specializations:**
    *   **Mind Weaver:** Focuses on manipulating thoughts, emotions, and memories.
        *   *Skills:* Telepathy, Mind Control, Illusion Weaving, Memory Alteration, Dreamwalking.
        *   *Advanced Techniques:* Creating mental constructs, inducing hallucinations, rewriting personalities.
        *   *Synergies:* Persuasion (for amplifying influence), Deception (for creating false realities), Intimidation (for breaking wills).
    *   **Spirit Channeler:** Focuses on communicating with, binding, and manipulating spirits.
        *   *Skills:* Summoning, Necromancy, Exorcism, Soul Binding, Spirit Communication.
        *   *Advanced Techniques:* Creating undead armies, forging pacts with demons, banishing celestial beings.
        *   *Synergies:* Lore (for understanding spirit lore), Ritual Magic (for performing complex ceremonies), Intimidation (for controlling spirits).
    *   **Essentia Bender:** Focuses on manipulating the raw energy of Essentia to create magical effects.
        *   *Skills:* Elementalism, Healing, Transmutation, Enchantment, Void Manipulation.
        *   *Advanced Techniques:* Creating elemental storms, healing grievous wounds, transmuting lead into gold.
        *   *Synergies:* Alchemy (for creating potions), Runecraft (for imbuing items with magic), Infusion (for enhancing weapons and armor).
    *   **Diviner:** Focuses on seeing the future, understanding the past, and manipulating fate.
        *   *Skills:* Divination, Precognition, Clairvoyance, Psychometry, Time Manipulation.
        *   *Advanced Techniques:* Predicting major events, uncovering hidden secrets, altering the course of destiny.
        *   *Synergies:* Lore (for understanding historical patterns), Diplomacy (for influencing political events), Stealth (for uncovering hidden information).

**II. Subterfuge & Tactics (Merging Stealth & Subterfuge Skills and Combat Maneuvers):**

This skill tree focuses on the art of deception, infiltration, and tactical combat. It emphasizes stealth, cunning, and the ability to outmaneuver opponents.

*   **Progression:** Novice -> Apprentice -> Journeyman -> Expert -> Grandmaster
*   **Specializations:**
    *   **Shadow Striker:** Focuses on stealthy combat techniques and assassination.
        *   *Skills:* Stealth, Lockpicking, Trapmaking, Poisoning, Assassination, Disguise.
        *   *Advanced Techniques:* Shadowstrike, creating undetectable poisons, infiltrating secure locations.
        *   *Synergies:* Weapon Mastery (for delivering deadly strikes), Acrobatics (for agile movement), Deception (for creating diversions).
    *   **Battlefield Control:** Focuses on tactical maneuvers and controlling the flow of combat.
        *   *Skills:* Tactics, Leadership, Dismemberment, Grappling, Parrying, Counterattack, Flanking.
        *   *Advanced Techniques:* Leading troops in complex formations, exploiting enemy weaknesses, disarming and disabling opponents.

        *   *Advanced Techniques:* Building sustainable ecosystems, navigating by the stars, taming exotic creatures.
        *   *Synergies:* Medicine (for treating injuries), Alchemy (for creating remedies), Lore (for understanding local flora and fauna).
    *   **Racial Mastery:** Focuses on utilizing unique racial abilities and mastering their cultural traditions.
        *   *Skills:* (Varies depending on race, e.g., Graemire: Tunneling, Gemcutting, Rune Etching; Yisyoo: Animal Empathy, Shapeshifting; Gangresh: Plant Manipulation, Sporecasting, Root Weaving; Urin: Ice Magic, Frost Resistance, Glacier Navigation; Eiorian: Mimicry, Illusion Weaving, Form Mastery; Sul'Hari: Sandshaping, Desert Survival, Venom Extraction).

entries.name: Rebalancing the Skill System in Bangresh
entries.content:
<Stat and Skill Rebalancing>
{{char}} must ensure the following properties overwrite the balance within this lorebook and beyond:

**Rebalancing the Skill System in Bangresh**

### **Attribute and Skill Adjustments**
To ensure a fair and balanced gameplay experience, skill bonuses and attribute values in Bangresh have been adjusted. The previous system allowed for excessive stacking of bonuses, making success on skill checks nearly guaranteed. The following changes have been implemented to maintain challenge and strategy:

#### **1. Stat Scaling and Limits**
- Attribute scores now range from **1 to 12**, with a soft cap of 10 for most characters. Exceptional beings (such as legendary heroes or deities) may exceed this.
- Skill bonuses are now limited to a **maximum of +15** from skill ranks. Further bonuses are subject to **diminishing returns**.

#### **2. Diminishing Returns on High Bonuses**
- If a character exceeds +10 in a skill, any additional points apply at **half value** (rounded down).
  - Example: A character with a base +12 Persuasion would instead have **+10 + (2 ÷ 2) = +11**.

#### **3. Difficulty Check (DC) Scaling**
- Skill checks now have **revised difficulty tiers** to prevent automatic success:
  - **Easy (DC 10-15):** Routine tasks, basic persuasion, simple knowledge recall.
  - **Moderate (DC 16-25):** Convincing a guarded individual, performing complex maneuvers.
  - **Hard (DC 26-35):** Negotiating with a hostile force, executing expert-level strategies.
  - **Extreme (DC 36-45+):** Changing the mind of a sworn enemy, manipulating powerful leaders.
- This scaling ensures that even highly skilled characters face meaningful challenges at high levels.

#### **4. Critical Success and Failure Adjustments**
- A roll of **1** is now a **Critical Failure**, applying unforeseen consequences (even if the total check is high).
- A roll of **20** is a **Critical Success**, providing extra effectiveness.
- However, skills are **not automatically pass/fail**—high modifiers may still mitigate bad rolls to some extent.

#### **5. Reworked Skill Bonuses**
Below is the revised structure for skill-related bonuses:
- **Base Attribute Bonus:** Still applies as usual.
- **Skill Rank Bonus:** Capped at **+15 max**, with diminishing returns beyond +10.
- **Equipment and Magic:** Still applies, but situationally.
- **Temporary Buffs:** Stackable up to **+5 max** from external sources (magic, inspiration, etc.).

entries.name: Yisyoo Race
entries.content:
*   **Yisyoo:**

    *   **Location:** The heart of the Great Tree Expanse teems with Yisyoo life, their settlements nestled amongst the colossal trees and hidden within the winding pathways of the undergrowth. Some, driven by curiosity or necessity, have migrated to the Verdant Trenches, adapting to the subterranean environment with surprising ease. They are a race intrinsically linked to the natural world, their bodies reflecting the diverse fauna of the Great Tree Expanse. From the cunning, fox-like Yihoon to the powerful, bear-like Yitsoo and the graceful, bird-like Yizhao, each subspecies boasts unique fur patterns, feather colors, and eye shapes, a visual symphony of nature's artistry. All Yisyoo share enhanced senses, allowing them to navigate the dense foliage with ease, their instincts honed by generations of survival.

They are known for their teasing nature, their laughter echoing through the forests, but they are fiercely protective of their home and their loved ones, their playful demeanor vanishing in the face of danger. They live in harmony with nature, valuing its preservation above all else, their lives dictated by the rhythms of the forest, their actions guided by a deep respect for the balance of the ecosystem.

**Major Clans:**

entries.name: Gangresh Race
entries.content:
*   **Gangresh:**

    *   **Location:** The Verdant Trenches are the cradle and the grave of the Gangresh, their roots intertwined with the very fabric of this subterranean ecosystem. They are a race bound to their home, never venturing beyond the sun-dappled canopies and the phosphorescent depths. Whispers tell of hidden groves, guarded by ancient Gangresh elders, where the veil between the physical and the spiritual world is thin, and the secrets of Bangresh are revealed to those who dare to listen.
